In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and use of a whole-body exposure system for the study of the upper respiratory tract and lungs of laboratory mice.
the development and application of aerosol exposure systems for use in the study of the pathogenesis of respiratory diseases in animals.
the use of aerosol systems to deliver infectious agents into the respiratory tract of laboratory animals.

nose-only aerosol exposure is a better method for inducing respiratory tract infections than is whole-body aerosol exposure.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nose-only exposure system is more efficient than the whole-body system for inducing infections in mice.
nose-only exposure is a more efficient aerosol delivery system than whole-body exposure for the induction of URT infections in mice.
nose-only exposure was superior to whole-body exposure in terms of reproducibility of results and the ability to detect the presence of pathogens in the respiratory tract.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nose-only aerosol exposure can be used to induce infections in mice.
nose-only aerosol exposure is a viable method for inducing respiratory disease in laboratory mice.
the nose-only system can be used as an effective method to deliver aerosolized pathogens to the upper respiratory tract and lungs of mice.
